text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London finished easier but fears over seasonal tightness lent a firm tone to the market, trade sources said. However, production and export figures so far do not point to a tight supply situation in the whites market. August closed $1.70 lower at $326.70 per tonne, while October lost $2.0 to close at $317.20 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed weaker as the trade and speculators sold amid a lack of interest by the funds. July closed 10 points lower at 11.47 cents/lb, while October gave up 11 points to close at 11.21 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 5 and 11 points. Traders said analysts are encouraged by the longer term fundamental outlook as the supply and demand balance tips in favor of the bulls. It was said that last week, the United States Department of Agriculture raised global demand by about 2 per cent while keeping output steady, for the 1997/98 season. Even though this points to a draw down of stocks, it should be noted, that global inventories are still quite high.

UKRAINE - Boris Supikhanov, deputy agriculture minister, told Reuters that sugar beet production in 1997 can be estimated at 24 million tonnes, the same as last year. The area sown to sugar beet this year has been reduced to 1.164 million ha, down from 1.418 million ha in 1996 to rein in surplus sugar production. Sugar production in 1997, including production of white sugar from imported raws, is officially expected to reach 3.26 million tonnes, white value, the same as in 1996, after 3.49 million tonnes in 1995.

Ukrainian agriculture minister Mykhailo Zubets said that Russian president Boris Yeltsin had promised to repeal Moscow's 20 per cent value-added tax (VAT) on imports of white sugar from the Ukraine. In addition to VAT, Russia also levies a 25 per cent import duty on imported Ukrainian sugar. Zubets also told a news conference that Russia planned to invest heavily in Ukraine's ageing factories. He added the Russians calculate that they will become co-owner in 170 of the country's 192 sugar factories. This comes as somewhat of a surprise, as the Russian sugar industry itself is in a very bad state and needs heavy investment to improve efficiency.

FRANCE - Sugar deliveries in December 1996 reached 148,763 tonnes, raw value, 1.8 per cent less than in the same month the previous year. That brought total consumption since the beginning of 1996/97 up to 451,508 tonnes which compares to 492,299 tonnes the same period in 1995. Total consumption in crop year 1995/96 rose to 2.220 million tonnes, up from 2.184 million tonnes in 1994/95. Sugar consumption in calendar year 1996 reached 2.269 million tonnes, up from 2.185 million tonnes the previous year.

NORWAY - Sugar imports in January/April 1997 reached 55,522 tonnes, raw value, slightly down on last year's figure of 56,259 tonnes. Total imports in 1996 reached 188,832 tonnes, 8.7 per cent more than in 1995. Main suppliers of white sugar in January/April 1997 were Denmark (26,010 vs 35,405 tonnes) and the United Kingdom (14,639 vs 13,567 tonnes).
